Hello, I'm Peter allow me to introduce myself. I am a technologist above all else. My experience whether personal or professional has lead me to touch all sorts of areas of tech. I've done some help desk work; setting up computers and printers. I've done some IoT work and networking. I've written programs that analyze complex data. I've even trained some AI models.

However, most of my experience lies in full-stack web development. I've built everything from user experiences that reach tens of thousands of people a month to interconnected systems that automate processes, and deliver complex content. The purpose of this site is to share the outcomes of projects I've had best to time working on.

Projects

  1. Legacy App Migration to a New Stack, Built with AI

    Personal

    A legacy photo-gallery app had 3 high-severity vulnerabilities in its upload dependencies, 9 packages it used but never declared, and failed to start on a clean install. I rebuilt it on a modern stack I had never used, with Claude as a partner, but made every design decision myself. I checked each result by hand, threw out two bad performance measurements, and confirmed deletes remove both the record and the stored file. Dependency checks now find 0 vulnerabilities, a fresh clone runs locally in 16 seconds with 13 commands, and compression cut CSS from 232 KB to 49 KB.

    Angular · ASP.NET Core · Azure Cosmos DB · Blob Storage · Claude | Source Baseline

  2. Agentic Removal of a Deprecated Feature

    A deprecated feature was still live in a production codebase that was slowing teams down with routine maintenance. I ran a multi-pass AI workflow: map every dependency, verify, send each scope question to a person, then delete. It caught multiple scope corrections the first estimate missed, and it kept files that a plain pattern-match would have wrongly removed. 300+ files came out in about half a day, in a stack of pull requests that all passed CI.

    Agentic Workflows · CI/CD · Code Migration

  3. AI Agent Skill for Design-System Update

    A team owned two dozen libraries with thousands of lines of code that had to move to the latest UI design system before the end of the quarter. We were given an AI skill that updated one library at a time. I built a wrapper skill around it that put every library on its own branch, generated a verification guide for each one, and added quality gates before review. I then handed the complex skill to an agentic workflow to run through the whole list. Per-library effort dropped from hours to near-zero, and the full set was done in about three weeks.

    Agentic Workflows · AI Agent Skills · Code Migration

  4. Multi-Ticket Lint Cleanup Pipeline

    Ran a multi-phase agentic workflow (spec, plan, implement, test, review, PR) to resolve dozens of linting violations across roughly ten interconnected projects ahead of a strict compliance deadline. Parallel implementation agents handled independently scoped work items, with independent verification so a shared-state regression never reached review. Result: a handful of clean, CI-passing PRs opened in about a day and merged the next, with every caveat disclosed.

    Agentic Workflows · Parallel Agents · CI/CD

  5. Law Firm Web Platform: Monolith to Headless

    A law firm's WordPress site was bloated, its home page graded D on GTmetrix, and it kept crashing due to hosting limits. I split the front end from the content server, put each on its own host, and set up monitoring and outage alerts on both. I also automated deploys and wrote a microservice for complex content delivery. With this new flexibility I was able to add email marketing and a CRM integration, which grew a new mailing list to 40+ subscribers in the first year. The home page grade went from D to A, uptime reached 99%, and hosting costs fell about 90%, which funded the new marketing integrations.

    Digital Ocean · Next.js · Node.js · Vercel · WordPress GraphQL · MySQL · GitHub Actions · Mailchimp · HubSpot | Site

  6. Asbury Park High School Hall of Fame: Redesign & Migration

    A non-profit high school Hall of Fame site had to be hand-coded page by page: adding one inductee meant editing up to 107 files, because the navigation was copied into every page. It also ran on plain HTTP, had no mobile layout, and still showed a four-year-old announcement. I scoped it, planned three phases, and rebuilt it with a member directory filterable by year, ceremony photo galleries, event and donation pages, and contact and nomination forms. All content lives in one small data file that generates every page, so there is no database to host or maintain. Adding an inductee now takes 1 file, accessibility rose from 53 to 96, SEO from 82 to 100, requires no hosting costs, and the site runs on HTTPS.

    Next.js · Cloudinary · Vercel · Accessibility · SEO | Baseline Results

  7. Unleashed Potential: Headless CMS Rebuild

    A life coach paid $20 a month for a Wix site and wanted to publish her own podcasts, interviews, and posts. I rebuilt it on a headless CMS so she can do that herself, then changed every content page from rendering on each visit to prebuilt pages, so the site keeps serving even if the CMS goes down. A later audit found a 3.6 MB hero photo and 150 known vulnerabilities, and I fixed both. Hosting fell from $240 a year to $8, Lighthouse performance rose from 73 to 88, and known runtime vulnerabilities went from 150 to 0.

    Next.js · TypeScript · Contentful CMS · SEO | Baseline Results

  8. CubbieKit: Shipping Label Automation

    Shopify store had a problem creating shipping labels for its orders. I designed the backend fix and led the build as lead engineer, running twice-weekly standups and tracking work in Linear. The new service reads orders from the store and creates labels automatically, and I tested it against the live store before launch. I then worked with customer service to automate return labels too, testing with sample orders. Labels for orders and returns are now created automatically, with no manual step.

    Node.js · Shopify GraphQL · Shippo · Heroku · Linear
